title.en: Sacred treasure of the Taiping kingdom

alt.en: The reverse of a square-holed coin bears the two characters sheng bao, “sacred treasure”; museum label, scale, colour chart and watermark remain visible.
alt.zh: 方孔钱背面铸“圣宝”二字；来源照片的藏品标签、标尺、色卡与水印均予保留。

caption.en: Reverse of a Taiping Tianguo coin, National Museum of History 78-01051. The obverse names the kingdom; the reverse calls its money “sacred treasure”. The exact mint and casting year are not recorded.
caption.zh: 国立历史博物馆78-01051号太平天国钱背面。正面列国号，背面称“圣宝”；具体铸地与铸造年份未载。

interpretation.en: Hong Xiuquan’s kingdom joined religious authority to government. The words “sacred treasure” put that claim onto money, complementing the religious publications discussed in his biography.
interpretation.zh: 洪秀全的政权将宗教权威与统治相结合。“圣宝”二字把这种宣示带到钱币上，与传记所述宗教出版物相互参照。

items.creator: Unidentified mint; museum photograph
items.date: Taiping period, 1851–1864; exact casting year unrecorded

title.en: Li Zicheng’s reign name on money
title.zh: 钱币上的李自成永昌年号

alt.en: A corroded round coin with a square hole and four raised characters, Yongchang tongbao; the museum label and colour scale remain below.
alt.zh: 圆形锈蚀钱币中央有方孔，四周铸“永昌通宝”；下方保留馆藏标签与色标。

caption.en: Yongchang tongbao, a five-cash denomination of Li Zicheng’s Shun regime, catalogued to 1644–1645. This example entered the National Museum of History in 1988.
caption.zh: 李自成大顺政权的永昌通宝折五钱，馆藏说明列铸行期为1644—1645年；本件1988年入藏国立历史博物馆。

interpretation.en: A new reign name made the claim to rule visible in an everyday object. The coin accompanies Li’s move from rebellion to state-building, while its five-cash denomination points to administration as well as conquest. Its findspot and individual mint are not recorded.
interpretation.zh: 新年号把统治主张铸进日常物件。此钱对应李自成由反叛走向建政的过程，折五面值也提示征服之外的行政需求；本件出土地与具体铸局未载。

items.date: Yongchang era, 1644–1645; individual casting year unrecorded

title.en: Han Lin’er’s Longfeng reign on a coin
title.zh: 钱币上的韩林儿龙凤年号

alt.en: A green-patinated square-holed coin reads Longfeng tongbao, with the museum number, scale, colour chart and watermark retained.
alt.zh: 带绿色锈层的方孔钱铸“龙凤通宝”，并保留馆藏编号、标尺、色卡与水印。

caption.en: Longfeng tongbao of Han Lin’er’s late-Yuan Song regime. The museum connects this coin type with Liu Futong’s enthronement of Han at Bozhou in 1355; this example’s exact casting year is not given.
caption.zh: 元末韩林儿宋政权的龙凤通宝。馆藏说明将这一钱种与1355年刘福通拥韩林儿于亳州称帝相连；本件具体铸年未载。

interpretation.en: The new regime asserted authority through its own calendar and coinage. The characters above and below the square hole name the Longfeng era; those at right and left read tongbao, “circulating treasure”.
interpretation.zh: 新政权通过自立年号与铸币宣示权威。方孔上下的文字组成“龙凤”年号，右左两字为“通宝”。

items.date: Longfeng era of Han Lin’er; after its inauguration in 1355; exact year unrecorded

title.en: The Yongli court’s name survives on money
title.zh: 钱币保存的永历朝廷年号

alt.en: A mottled green-brown coin with a square hole bears Yongli tongbao; the photograph retains accession label, colour chart, scale and watermark.
alt.zh: 绿褐相间的方孔钱铸“永历通宝”；照片保留馆藏标签、色卡、标尺与水印。

caption.en: Yongli tongbao with gong on the reverse, catalogued to the Yongli coinage of 1647–1662. Zhu Youlang was enthroned at Zhaoqing in 1646 and named the following year Yongli 1.
caption.zh: 背面有“工”字的永历通宝，馆藏说明列铸行期为1647—1662年。朱由榔1646年在肇庆即位，以次年为永历元年。

interpretation.en: A reign name on money carried the Southern Ming court’s claim beyond a palace proclamation. This coin illustrates the political authority associated with Yongli, rather than the accession ceremony itself. Its precise mint and findspot are not established in this catalog.
interpretation.zh: 钱币上的年号，把南明朝廷的政治主张带出宫廷宣告的场合。本件表现与永历相连的统治权威，而非即位仪式本身；馆藏记录未确定其具体铸局与出土地。

items.creator: Unidentified mint; museum photograph
items.date: Yongli coinage, 1647–1662; exact casting year unrecorded

title.zh: 永历通宝：即位与改元的年代

contextSources.publisher: Tainan City Cultural Affairs Bureau, via Taiwan Cultural Memory Bank

title.en: Li Zicheng · rebellion, relief and a brief capital
title.zh: 李自成 · 反叛、赈济与短暂占都

summary.en: Li Zicheng joined Gao Yingxiang’s forces in 1631 and became a leading rebel commander after Gao’s execution in 1636. Famine and the promise of relief helped enlarge his following in Henan; military victory also required turning seized resources into administration. At Xiangyang and then Xi’an, his movement began building the institutions of a rival state. In 1644 he adopted the dynastic name Shun and captured Beijing as Ming authority collapsed. Success lasted only briefly. Wu Sangui’s forces and the Manchus defeated him at Shanhai Pass, forcing a retreat from the capital. His trajectory connects the desperation of regional rebellion with the different demands of holding and governing an empire.
summary.zh: 1631年李自成加入高迎祥部，1636年高被处死后，李成为主要反叛统帅。河南饥荒与救济的许诺扩大了追随者队伍；军事胜利同时要求把夺得的资源转化为行政能力。在襄阳、继而西安，其势力开始建立与明朝竞争的国家机构。1644年李自成采用大顺国号，在明廷崩溃时攻入北京，但占都仅维持短暂时期。吴三桂军与满洲军在山海关击败他，迫其撤出都城。李的经历连接了地方反叛中的生存困境，以及占有、治理帝国所面临的不同要求。

dateNote.en: 1631–1644 is the selected period of documented activity, not a lifespan. Dates are given at civil-year precision; map points are representative.
dateNote.zh: 1631—1644年为所选有据活动时期，并非生卒年。日期精度为公元年；地图点为代表位置。

sources.evidenceNoteZh: 1631年加入高部、1636年接续、河南赈济、襄阳行政及1644年北京—山海关过程。

description.zh: 进入规模更大的反叛联盟。

title.en: Hong Xiuquan · religious texts and a rival kingdom
title.zh: 洪秀全 · 宗教文本与另立王国

summary.en: Hong Xiuquan reinterpreted earlier visions after reading Christian tracts in 1843, coming to believe that he was Jesus’s younger brother. Preaching in Guangxi helped create the religious movement that became the Taiping challenge to Qing rule. After taking Nanjing in 1853, the Taiping made it their capital, Tianjing, and issued religious instructions alongside plans for government and land. Their publications are evidence of aspirations and prescribed order, not proof that every programme was implemented. Hong’s regime also suffered violent leadership struggles, including the killings of 1856. He died in 1864 before Qing forces captured the capital. His story links the circulation of printed religion to mass mobilization, civil war and contested political authority.
summary.zh: 1843年洪秀全阅读基督教传教书后，重新解释早年的异象，自认为耶稣之弟。在广西的传教活动，促成了后来挑战清朝的太平天国运动。1853年太平军攻取南京，改为都城天京，发布宗教训诫，也提出治理与土地制度方案。这些出版物反映理想和规定秩序，不能据此认定每项方案都已实行。其政权还经历了1856年等暴力领导权斗争。洪秀全于1864年清军攻陷都城之前去世。他的故事把宗教印刷品的流通，与群众动员、内战和政治权威之争联系起来。

dateNote.en: 1843–1864 is the selected period of documented activity, not a lifespan. Dates are given at civil-year precision; map points are representative.
dateNote.zh: 1843—1864年为所选有据活动时期，并非生卒年。日期精度为公元年；地图点为代表位置。

description.zh: 太平天国将南京改称天京。

description.en: He died before Qing troops captured the capital.
description.zh: 在清军攻取都城之前去世。

# China batch 12: political authority on coins

Ready shard: visual-assets-china-batch-12-v18.json (4 assets, 4 unique uncovered targets).
Copy map: asset-copy-manifest.json. Reference draft: references/media/china-batch-12.md.
No production edits, commit, push, upload or Actions.

## Evidence and review

Each accepted record has *-source.html, *-source.txt, *-receipt.json, and both coin faces downloaded unchanged. The accepted photographs are taiping-1.jpg (reverse), yongchang-0.jpg, longfeng-0.jpg and yongli-0.jpg. Actual pixels were inspected in review.jpg. All four show readable relevant characters, accession labels, source watermarks and calibration scales; these are preserved. Images are 426×640 and 40–55KB, adequate but lower resolution than NPM derivatives. They are not cropped or enlarged. Reverse-side references in captions come from the item records and preserved counterpart photographs.

Item pages explicitly show CC BY 3.0 TW+ alongside each accepted image, not only at record level. Credits preserve the requested object title and Culture Ministry attribution and add the holding National Museum of History. Exact downloaded URLs, sizes and hashes are in receipts/shard. The museum catalog does not establish mint/findspot or individual year, and the captions do not invent them.

Full target records are preserved in target-records.json. Hong and Li are reviewed biographies. Longfeng museum context explicitly states Liu Futong enthroned Han Lin’er at Bozhou in 1355, named Song and the Longfeng era; the image is a regime coin, not coronation evidence. The inherited title’s Xiaomingwang epithet is not used in the image caption. Yongli context independently dates accession at Zhaoqing to 24 December 1646 and the first era year to 1647; source HTML/text preserved. That separate contextual item has restricted images, none fetched or reused.

## Rejected or not admitted

- Zhang Juzheng, TCMB 19000000245: record-level CC BY is contradicted by image-specific restricted-public-view labels. Not admitted. Automatically retrieved preview files removed. Receipt retained as audit only; no images for reuse.
- Jiang Wei theatrical figure, TCMB 20000017369: same image-specific restriction despite record-level CC BY. Not admitted. Automatically retrieved previews removed. Receipt retained as audit only. This is also a modern dramatic characterization rather than a historical likeness.
- LOC 2008660408 and 00651039 metadata requests returned HTTP403. The batch was stopped; no alternate route or image retrieval attempted. These remain denied sources.
- Zhaowu coin 77-00143, TCMB 14000138572: image rights and pixels pass. Potential target landmark140 bundles Wu Sangui’s 1678 enthronement/death with Qing reconquest of Hunan; the latter timing is not verified here. Hold association until record is repaired or fully verified. Source and both images retained for possible future research. Do not map to the 1644 Shanhai Pass event.
- Dashun coin 83-01796, TCMB 14000141217: image rights and pixels pass, but it is Zhang Xianzhong’s Daxi-era currency (1644–1646), NOT Li Zicheng’s Shun currency. No current exact clean target found. The 1643 compound ming039 entry does not represent its issue. No admission.
- TCMB 107000030534 Li Zicheng coin and the ceramic Zhao Yun/Jiang Wei objects surfaced in search carry CC BY-NC; not fetched/admitted.

## Scope limits

No image is mapped across unrelated battles simply because a ruler or regime is named. In particular, Taiping currency is attached only to Hong’s religious-political biography, not to the Jintian uprising, capture/siege of Nanjing or leadership killings. The Longfeng coin is not used for the earlier 1351 uprising. Four unique targets is the defensible yield of this batch, not a broad coverage-padding exercise.
